fullPassage:
"Selena. SELENA!"
"Yes," I look up from my phone to discover my mom yelling at me. She seems to be searching for an answer to something. "What?" I asked.
She asked, "Did you not hear what I just said?"
No, I didn't. I didn't hear anything she said. I usually don't hear a single word said to me by anyone. And why is that? It's because my eyes are fixed on my phone. My mom always asks me, "What is so interesting on your phone?" I never know how to answer that because even I don't know what's so interesting on my phone.
I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear missing out on social media. I fear not being in the know of what everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know of what my friends are posting on social media.
My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to social media. It's an addiction to being online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.
Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure. Maybe this spring break could be a chance to find one.

So it was time to pull the plug.
I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons dotting the screen. I removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of the social media sites. I felt an immediate sense of relief.
But soon after, I got restless. I don't remember how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen in complete confusion for quite a while. I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But there's only so much you can do over a voice call. We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a bike ride.
What else can I do on my phone? I lay on my bed even though I wasn't sleepy. I stayed there until I went out to meet Jamie. Throughout the day, it felt like things slowed down considerably. What a long day!

I woke up late in the morning and reached for my phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember my social media apps were no longer there. Old habits die hard. After breakfast, I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn't want to give in. So, I decided to go out for a walk.
While walking in the park, I probably glanced at my phone 20 times. At one moment, I looked at the people around me, most of whom had their eyes glued to their phones. I moved my gaze upward and noticed how purely blue the sky was, without a single cloud in sight. All around the park, trees slowly swayed back and forth. Soon I found myself taking a couple of pictures of the peaceful scene.
After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn't matter that I'm not really good at it. It just felt great that I was lost in doing something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone.

I don't know why, but today I momentarily let down my guard against social media. As if bound by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites, only to find that there was nothing interesting. I had a weird feeling of being at a place where I didn't belong, which was quickly replaced by a sense of guilt. I really shouldn't have gone back to a social media site in the middle of my detox.

This was the first day my phone felt more like a brick in my pocket than a digital device. I could already feel free from worrying about posting something and hoping it would get some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get asked over and over again about how I was surviving without social media. Sam said, "I don't think I could give up social media for even one day." My immediate thought was: Then you really need to give it up! I didn't actually say that, although I wanted to.

Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social media break and what things had been like before. I realized that social media had taken some control of me. It's kind of silly that all I did was envy others for their perfectly happy moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and think up ways to get others to like my posts.
From now on, I want to be in control of how I use something or do something, not the other way around. Tomorrow, I will return to my social media activities, but in more careful and controlled ways. I'm going to stick to just a couple of sites that I really need, while making absolutely sure that my activities are in line with my well-being and happiness.

questions.passage: I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear missing out on social media. __________. Maybe this spring break could be a chance to find one.
questions.stem: 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오. a cure / I have / basically / severe FOMO / need of / in desperate / for which / I'm
questions.wa: Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure
accept: Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure
Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure.

det.korean: 근본적으로, 나는 심한 FOMO를 겪고 있는데, 치료법이 절실히 필요한 상태다.
det.analysis: Basically(근본적으로) + I have severe FOMO(심한 FOMO를 겪고 있다) + for which(그것에 대해) + I'm in desperate need of(절실히 필요하다) + a cure(치료법). 관계대명사 for which가 FOMO를 선행사로 받음
det.tip: for which = ~에 대해(관계대명사). in desperate need of = ~이 절실히 필요한. 전치사+관계대명사 구문이 핵심

questions.ans: Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure

questions.passage: I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not ①<u>checking</u> my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear ②<u>missing</u> out on social media. I fear not being in the know of ③<u>what</u> everyone is discussing. I fear not being in the know of what my friends are ④<u>post</u> on social media.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 친구들이 소셜 미디어에 무엇을 올리는지(posting) 모르는 게 두렵다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ post → posting: 'are posting'은 현재진행형. be동사 are 뒤에 동사원형 post는 올 수 없음
❌ ① checking: 전치사 from 뒤 동명사. 'from not checking' 정상
❌ ② missing: fear + -ing. 'fear missing out' 정상
❌ ③ what: 간접의문문 what everyone is discussing. what이 discussing의 목적어 역할
det.tip: be + V-ing = 진행형. are posting(올리고 있는). be + 원형은 수동태(be + p.p.)나 조동사 뒤에서만 가능

questions.passage: So it was time to pull the plug. I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons ①<u>dotting</u> the screen. I removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved to my notebook computer. I ②<u>was logged</u> out of all of the social media sites. I felt an ③<u>immediate</u> sense of relief. But soon after, I got ④<u>restless</u>.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 나는 모든 소셜 미디어 사이트에서 로그아웃했다(logged out).
det.analysis:
✅ ② was logged → logged: 원문은 'I logged out'(능동). 스스로 로그아웃한 것이므로 수동태 was logged는 부적절
❌ ① dotting: 현재분사의 후치수식. 'icons dotting the screen'(화면에 흩어진 아이콘들) 정상
❌ ③ immediate: 명사 sense 앞 형용사. 정상
❌ ④ restless: 'got restless'에서 got(~하게 되다)의 보어로 형용사. 정상
det.tip: 능동 vs 수동: 주어가 직접 행동하면 능동(logged out), 당하는 것이면 수동(was logged out). 여기서는 화자가 직접 로그아웃함

questions.passage: After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up ①<u>playing</u> it all afternoon. It didn't matter that I'm not really good at it. It just felt great that I was lost in ②<u>doing</u> something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone. I don't know why, but today I momentarily let down my guard against social media. As if ③<u>binding</u> by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites, only ④<u>to find</u> that there was nothing interesting.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 부분 중 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: 마치 주문에 묶인 것처럼(bound) 소셜 미디어 사이트에 로그인했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ binding → bound: 'As if bound by a spell'에서 주어(I)가 주문에 의해 묶이는 것이므로 수동의 과거분사 bound 필요. binding(현재분사/능동)은 '묶는'이 되어 의미 부적절
❌ ① playing: end up + -ing(결국 ~하게 되다). 정상
❌ ② doing: be lost in + -ing(~에 몰두하다). 정상
❌ ④ to find: only to + V(결국 ~하게 되다, 기대와 다른 결과). 정상
det.tip: as if + p.p. = 마치 ~된 것처럼 (수동). bind-bound-bound. as if bound by(~에 의해 묶인 듯) vs as if binding(~을 묶는 듯)

questions.passage: I grabbed my phone. I swiped it open and stared at the social media icons ①<u>dotting</u> the screen. I removed the apps from my phone. Then I moved to my notebook computer. I logged out of all of the social media sites. I felt an immediate sense of ②<u>tension</u>. But soon after, I got ③<u>restless</u>. I stared at my phone screen in complete ④<u>confusion</u> for quite a while.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 모든 소셜 미디어 사이트에서 로그아웃한 후 즉시 안도감(relief)을 느꼈다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② tension → relief: 원문은 'I felt an immediate sense of relief'. 앱 삭제+로그아웃 후 느낀 감정은 안도(relief)이지 긴장(tension)이 아님
❌ ① dotting: 원문 일치. 화면에 흩어져 있는 아이콘들
❌ ③ restless: 원문 일치. 안도감 후 곧 안절부절못하게 됨
❌ ④ confusion: 원문 일치. 완전히 혼란스러운 상태
det.tip: relief(안도) ↔ tension(긴장). 문맥의 흐름: 앱 삭제 → 안도 → 안절부절 → 혼란. 첫 반응이 안도라는 점이 핵심

questions.passage: This was the first day my phone felt more like a brick in my pocket than a ①<u>digital</u> device. I could already feel free from ②<u>worrying</u> about posting something and hoping it would get some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get asked over and over again about how I was ③<u>thriving</u> without social media. Sam said, "I don't think I could ④<u>give up</u> social media for even one day."
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 단어 중 문맥상 부적절한 것은?

det.korean: 소셜 미디어 없이 어떻게 살아남고(surviving) 있는지 질문을 받는 게 재미있었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ thriving → surviving: 원문은 'surviving without social media'. thriving(번영하는/잘 살아가는)은 지나치게 긍정적. 친구들이 놀라며 묻는 맥락에서 surviving(간신히 살아남는)이 적절
❌ ① digital: 원문 일치. '디지털 기기보다 벽돌 같은'
❌ ② worrying: 원문 일치. '게시물 걱정에서 자유로워졌다'
❌ ④ give up: 원문 일치. '소셜 미디어를 포기하다'
det.tip: surviving(살아남는: 힘든 상황에서 버티는) vs thriving(번영하는: 잘 해나가는). 친구들의 놀란 반응에는 '어떻게 살아남느냐'가 더 자연스러움

questions.passage: My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a __________. It's an addiction to social media. It's an addiction to being online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 나는 이것이 기기(device) 중독이 아니라고 말하겠다. 소셜 미디어 중독이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① device(기기): 원문 일치. 'addiction to a device'가 아니라 'addiction to social media'라는 대조 구문
❌ ② website(웹사이트): social media보다 좁은 개념. 대조가 약해짐
❌ ③ person(사람): 사람에 대한 중독은 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ④ habit(습관): 습관 중독이라는 표현은 자연스럽지 않음
det.tip: device(기기) vs social media: 화자는 기기 자체가 아니라 소셜 미디어 사용이 중독이라고 구분. phones and computers(기기) ↔ social media(소프트웨어/서비스)

questions.passage: Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social media break and what things had been like before. I realized that social media had taken some control of me. It's kind of silly that all I did was envy others for their perfectly happy moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and think up ways to get others to like my posts. From now on, I want to be in control of how I use something or do something, not the other way around. I'm going to stick to just a couple of sites that I really need, while making absolutely sure that my activities are __________ my well-being and happiness.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 내 활동이 확실히 내 웰빙과 행복에 관련이 있도록(in line with) 할 것이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② in line with(~에 부합하는): 원문 일치. 활동이 웰빙/행복과 일치하도록 하겠다는 통제 의지
❌ ① in charge of(~를 담당하는): 활동이 웰빙을 담당한다는 표현은 부자연스러움
❌ ③ at odds with(~와 충돌하는): 반대 의미. 활동이 웰빙과 충돌하면 화자의 의도와 모순
❌ ④ in need of(~이 필요한): 활동이 웰빙이 필요하다는 것은 논리적이지 않음
det.tip: in line with = ~에 부합하는/일치하는. at odds with = ~와 충돌하는 (반의 표현). in line with one's goals/values 형태로 자주 사용

questions.passage: My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to social media. It's an addiction to being online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 화자의 엄마는 화자가 건강하게 폰을 사용한다고 생각한다.
화자는 기기 중독이 아니라 소셜 미디어 중독이라고 말한다.
어른들은 십대들이 폰에 관심이 없다고 생각한다.
화자는 온라인에 접속하지 않는 것을 즐긴다.

det.korean: 기기가 아닌 소셜 미디어에 대한 중독이라고 화자가 직접 밝힘
det.analysis:
✅ ② 원문 일치: 'I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to social media.'
❌ ① 반대: 엄마는 'addicted to my phone'이라고 생각함 (부정적)
❌ ③ 반대: 어른들은 'have an addiction'이라고 생각함
❌ ④ 반대: 'a fear of not being online'(온라인이 아닌 것에 대한 두려움)
det.tip: addiction to a device(기기 중독) vs addiction to social media(소셜 미디어 중독) — 화자가 명확히 구분

questions.passage: I woke up late in the morning and reached for my phone. I swiped my phone open only to remember my social media apps were no longer there. Old habits die hard. After breakfast, I felt a strong urge to go online, to which I didn't want to give in. So, I decided to go out for a walk.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
ch: 소셜 미디어 앱이 여전히 폰에 남아 있었다.

det.korean: 온라인 충동에 굴복하지 않고 산책을 나가기로 결정했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 일치: 'I decided to go out for a walk'
❌ ① 반대: 'woke up late in the morning'(늦게 일어남)
❌ ② 반대: 'social media apps were no longer there'(앱이 더 이상 없었음)
❌ ③ 반대: 'didn't want to give in'(굴복하고 싶지 않았다)
det.tip: give in to = ~에 굴복하다. 'didn't want to give in' = 굴복하고 싶지 않았다 → 실제로 굴복하지 않음

questions.passage: But soon after, I got restless. I don't remember how long it was, but I stared at my phone screen in complete confusion for quite a while. I called Jamie, and we chatted for about an hour. But there's only so much you can do over a voice call. We decided to meet later in the afternoon for a bike ride.
questions.stem: 위 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
ch: 앱 삭제 후 곧 안절부절못하게 되었다.
Jamie와 약 한 시간 정도 통화했다.
음성 통화로 할 수 있는 일에는 한계가 있다.
Jamie와 아침에 자전거를 타러 만나기로 했다.

det.korean: 오후에(afternoon) 만나기로 했지, 아침(morning)이 아니다.
det.analysis:
✅ ④ 불일치: 원문은 'later in the afternoon'인데 진술은 '아침에'
❌ ① 일치: 'soon after, I got restless'
❌ ② 일치: 'we chatted for about an hour'
❌ ③ 일치: 'there's only so much you can do over a voice call'
det.tip: in the afternoon(오후에) ≠ in the morning(아침에). 시간 세부 정보 변조는 내신 빈출 함정

questions.passage: I have a bad case of anxiety that comes from not checking my phone. I spend most of my day on social media. I fear missing out on social media. Basically, I have severe FOMO, for which I'm in desperate need of a cure. So it was time to pull the plug.
questions.stem: 위 글의 주제로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 소셜 미디어 중독(FOMO)으로 인한 불안과 디톡스의 시작

det.korean: FOMO(놓치는 것의 두려움)로 인한 불안 → 디톡스를 시작하겠다는 결심
det.analysis:
✅ ① 주제: anxiety + FOMO + need of a cure + pull the plug → 중독의 고백과 디톡스 시작
❌ ② 기술 발전: 본문은 기술 비판이 아닌 개인 경험
❌ ③ 세대 갈등: 엄마 언급은 도입부일 뿐 주제가 아님
❌ ④ 시간 관리: 본문 주제와 무관
det.tip: pull the plug = 플러그를 뽑다 → 비유적으로 '중단하다/끊다'. FOMO의 심각성을 인식하고 행동에 나서는 전환점

questions.passage: This was the first day my phone felt more like <u>a brick in my pocket</u> than a digital device. I could already feel free from worrying about posting something and hoping it would get some likes. At a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get asked over and over again about how I was surviving without social media.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 'a brick in my pocket'이 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 휴대 전화가 물리적으로 무거워져서 주머니에 부담이 되었다.
소셜 미디어 앱 없이 휴대 전화가 쓸모없고 무의미하게 느껴졌다.
화자가 휴대 전화 대신 벽돌을 주머니에 넣고 다녔다.
휴대 전화의 배터리가 방전되어 사용할 수 없었다.

det.korean: 소셜 미디어 앱을 삭제한 후 전화기가 벽돌처럼 쓸모없게 느껴졌다는 비유
det.analysis:
✅ ② 쓸모없고 무의미: brick(벽돌)은 무겁고 단순한 물건의 비유. 소셜 미디어 없는 폰은 디지털 기기로서의 기능을 상실한 듯한 느낌
❌ ① 물리적 무게: 비유적 표현이지 실제 무게 변화가 아님
❌ ③ 실제 벽돌: 비유를 문자 그대로 해석한 오류
❌ ④ 배터리 방전: 본문에 배터리 언급 없음. 기능적 무용이 아닌 심리적 무용
det.tip: brick은 '무겁고 쓸모없는 물건'의 대표적 비유. 'more like A than B' = B보다 A에 더 가까운. 디지털 기기라기보다 벽돌 같다 = 기능이 없는 것처럼 느낌

questions.passage: I don't know why, but today I momentarily let down my guard against social media. As if bound by a spell, I logged into one of the social media sites. There was nothing interesting on any of the pages I visited. I had a weird feeling of being at a place where I didn't belong, <u>which</u> was quickly replaced by a sense of guilt. I really shouldn't have gone back to a social media site in the middle of my detox.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 which가 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: 소속되지 않은 곳에 있다는 이상한 기분

det.korean: 소속되지 않은 곳에 있다는 이상한 기분(a weird feeling)이 죄책감으로 대체되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 이상한 기분: which의 선행사는 바로 앞의 'a weird feeling of being at a place where I didn't belong'. 이 기분이 죄책감으로 대체됨
❌ ① 소셜 미디어 사이트: 사이트가 죄책감으로 대체된다는 것은 논리적 부적합
❌ ② 발견: 'nothing interesting'은 앞의 별도 절
❌ ④ 디톡스 중간: 시간 표현이 감정으로 대체되지 않음
det.tip: which의 선행사 찾기: which 앞의 가장 가까운 명사/구를 찾되, 의미적으로 '대체되었다(replaced)'의 주어가 될 수 있는지 확인

questions.passage: This was the first day my phone felt more like a brick in my pocket than a digital device. I could already feel free from worrying about posting something. At a gathering with my friends, it was fun to get asked over and over again about how I was surviving without social media. Sam said, "I don't think I could give up social media for even one day." My immediate thought was: Then you really need to give <u>it</u> up! I didn't actually say that, although I wanted to.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 it이 가리키는 것으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Sam이 '소셜 미디어를 포기할 수 없다'고 해서 '그것(= 소셜 미디어)을 포기해야 한다'고 생각
det.analysis:
✅ ② 소셜 미디어: Sam의 말 'give up social media'에서 social media를 it으로 받음. 'give it up' = 소셜 미디어를 포기하다
❌ ① 모임: give up a gathering은 문맥에 맞지 않음
❌ ③ 휴대 전화: Sam이 언급한 것은 social media
❌ ④ 생각: give up a thought는 맥락 부적합
det.tip: 대명사 it은 가장 가까운 선행사를 받음. Sam: 'give up social media' → 화자: 'give it up' → it = social media

questions.passage: Toward the end of the day, I reflected on my social media break and what things had been like before. I realized that social media had taken some control of me. It's kind of silly that all I did was envy others for their perfectly happy moments in life, dress up my everyday events, and think up ways to get others to like my posts.
questions.stem:
위 글에서 다음 빈칸에 들어갈 **영어** 단어를 찾아 쓰시오.

'소셜 미디어가 화자를 어느 정도 __________했다는 것을 깨달았다.'

det.korean: 소셜 미디어가 나를 어느 정도 통제(control)했다는 것을 깨달았다.
det.analysis: 원문: 'social media had taken some control of me' → '통제했다'에 해당하는 단어는 control
det.tip: take control of = ~를 통제하다/장악하다. had taken(과거완료) = 이전부터 통제해 왔음을 암시

questions.passage: My mom thinks I'm addicted to my phone. Older people think teenagers like me have an addiction to their phones and computers. But I wouldn't say it's an addiction to a device. It's an addiction to __________ (be) online, or in other words, a fear of not being online.
questions.stem: 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오.

det.korean: 그것은 온라인에 있는 것(being online)에 대한 중독이다.
det.analysis: be → being. 전치사 to 뒤에 동명사(-ing) 형태가 와야 함. 'addiction to being online' = 온라인 상태에 있는 것에 대한 중독. to부정사의 to가 아닌 전치사 to
det.tip: addiction to + -ing: to가 전치사이므로 뒤에 동명사. look forward to + -ing, be used to + -ing와 같은 패턴. to부정사가 아님에 주의

questions.passage: After lunch, I took out my old guitar from under my bed. At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up playing it all afternoon. It didn't matter that I'm not really good at it. It just felt great that I was lost in doing something for several hours without getting interrupted by my phone.
questions.stem: 위 글에서 알 수 있는 것은?
ch: 화자는 점심 후 친구를 만나러 나갔다.
화자는 지루해서 기타를 꺼냈지만 결국 오후 내내 연주했다.
화자는 기타를 치는 동안 휴대 전화를 자주 확인했다.

det.korean: 심심해서 꺼냈지만 결국 오후 내내 기타를 치게 되었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 일치: 'At first, it was because I was bored, but I ended up playing it all afternoon'
❌ ① 반대: 'I'm not really good at it'(기타 실력이 별로)
❌ ② 반대: 점심 후 기타를 꺼냈지 외출하지 않았음
❌ ④ 반대: 'without getting interrupted by my phone'(폰에 방해 받지 않고)
det.tip: end up + -ing = 결국 ~하게 되다. 원래 의도와 다른 결과를 나타내는 표현

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 쓰시오.

'오래된 습관은 쉽게 없어지지 않는다.'

Old habits __________.

det.korean: 오래된 습관은 잘 없어지지 않는다(die hard).
det.analysis: 'Old habits die hard'는 관용 표현. die hard = 쉽게 사라지지 않다/고치기 어렵다. 본문에서 소셜 미디어 앱이 없는데도 습관적으로 폰을 여는 상황에 사용
det.tip: die hard = (습관/전통 등이) 쉽게 없어지지 않다. old habits die hard는 매우 흔한 영어 속담/관용구

questions.stem:
다음 우리말과 일치하도록 빈칸에 알맞은 말을 쓰시오.

'어쩌면 이번 봄 방학이 (치료법을) 찾을 기회가 될지도 모르겠다.'

Maybe this spring break could be a __________ to find one.

det.korean: 이번 봄 방학이 치료법을 찾을 기회(chance)가 될지도 모른다.
det.analysis: a chance to + V = ~할 기회. 'a chance to find one'에서 one은 앞의 cure를 대신하는 대명사
det.tip: chance to + V = ~할 기회. opportunity to와 동의. could be = ~일 수도 있다 (가능성)
